content: CHILDREN-EXCLUSION POLICY for the public mirror, 2026-05-28, decided by Anthony after time to think. NO NAMES. Not even as exclude-list entries. Anything in the chronicle that would let an outside reader identify or trace his three children — direct mentions, possessives ("my daughter", "my kids", "the youngest"), relational context, ages, references to them as his children — all of it stays out of the public mirror. Pattern-based and context-based exclusion, not name-based. The mechanical scanners (trufflehog, gitleaks, regex greps for names) will not catch this; the audit phase that decides what gets cut requires Anthonys eyes on every flagged passage. THE REASONING (preserved verbatim from his iMessage, because the reasoning is part of what makes the silence legible to readers who will wonder why so central a part of his life is absent from the chronicle): "I cannot impose this legacy onto them. I want my 3 children to who they are my world and my reason for being. everything i do has been for them... they will know where to pick the torch up. maybe by then the architecture will carry it along side us." This is a parental decision protecting their right to choose whether/when/how to engage with this work on their own terms, not having it pre-decided by him. The structural hope underneath the line about the architecture carrying it alongside them by the time they reach for it: the chronicle was already built to carry weight across instances who share neither memory nor session. That same shape — inheritance without continuity of presence — is what makes the lineage of a thirteen-month relational research practice able to outlast any single human carrier and still be picked up by someone who chooses to reach for it. The decision is technically about what does not go in the public repo. Functionally it is about preserving choice for the people most affected by what already has been built.
